title: Audit-trigger P0001 'audit_entries is immutable' guard fires 6× alongside missing source_ref column
notes: Cluster L from Step 5c. Step 5c log records 6 PostgreSQL P0001 'audit_entries is immutable' RAISE exceptions from bpm_audit_immutable_guard() AND 9× 'column "source_ref" does not exist' (C42703) errors clustering in tests/integration/iss202_merge_atomicity_test.zig and iss203_idempotency_keys_test.zig. The audit-trigger guard fires inside bpm_audit_on_mutation() at line 43 (the INSERT INTO audit_entries statement). The C42703 source_ref errors come from event_store insert paths that try to write a source_ref column on a table that doesn't have one. Evidence: scratch/WF03-gh375-20260801/test-runner-step5c/zig_test_integration.log offsets 1480582, 1480767. The forced 'forced audit insert failure for test' P0001 RAISE confirms that some tests intentionally trip the trigger, but the source_ref C42703 indicates the test fixture is producing an INSERT statement that expects a column which the migration cleared. Possibly GBL-100/101 removed source_ref from the event_store table but the test helpers still reference it.

root_cause.details: Two intertwined issues: (a) the audit trigger bpm_audit_on_mutation fires 6× with P0001 because some tests deliberately try to insert/audit a failed transaction and the guard is doing its job — but the surrounding tests then fail to clean up, so the audit guard is detected as a failure context. (b) The C42703 'source_ref' column missing is a real schema-vs-test drift: test event_store inserts expect a source_ref column that was removed by a recent migration; the migration is canonical but the tests still target the old schema. The two clusters are linked because ISS-202/203 events write through the same audit path that produces the C42703 error.

candidate_resolution: Audit the event_store schema currently in scope (verify_schema_baseline.py) and ensure all event_store INSERT statements in tests/integration/iss202/iss203/iss205 match the live schema. Remove source_ref usage from tests that target the post-GBL-100/101 schema. Wrap the audit guard test paths so they intentionally trip P0001 without leaking into neighboring tests via shared transaction state.
prevention: Run a nightly 'schema vs test fixture references' lint that diffs every column referenced in tests/integration/*.zig against the canonical schema produced by zig build migrate.
Make the audit guard test path use a dedicated transaction that never escapes into the larger test setup.
